stem: Meena opens the lid of a pressure cooker in her kitchen in Jaipur, and the steam quickly spreads throughout the room. Which statement correctly explains why a gas, like this steam, does not have a fixed shape or a fixed volume?

options.text: Gas particles have a fixed shape but move slowly, so the gas takes the shape of its container.
Gas particles move freely in all directions and the forces of attraction between them are negligible, so the gas spreads to fill all the available space.
Gas particles are tightly packed together, so the gas expands when the lid is opened.
Gas is mostly empty space, so steam spreads by itself without the particles needing to move.

teacher.key_rationale: A gas has no fixed shape or volume because its particles move freely in all directions with negligible interparticle attraction, so they spread to fill the available space. A is wrong because gas particles have no fixed shape and move rapidly; C is wrong because gas particles are far apart, not tightly packed; D restates the common misconception that empty space alone (without moving particles) explains spreading.
